canonical_name: Lucas-Lehmer primality criterion for Mersenne numbers
literal_source_claim_en: A fast test for Mersenne primes.
source_attribution: Edouard Lucas/Derrick Lehmer, 1930 (catalog metadata only; no cited work or passage)
canonical_statement: Candidate intake scope: for every natural p with 3 <= p, the zero-based Lucas-Lehmer residue after p - 2 updates from seed 4 modulo 2^p - 1 is zero if and only if the Mersenne number 2^p - 1 is prime.
canonical_claim: For p at least 3, the Lucas-Lehmer test accepts p exactly when the Mersenne number 2^p - 1 is prime; source-domain and indexing transport remain unaccepted.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only a performance-flavored gloss. Before the exact statement gate, an independent reviewer must approve an immutable source theorem and its complete proof/correction boundary; choose odd-prime versus all-natural p >= 3 scope; map one-based S_(p-1) to zero-based residue p-2; choose divisibility, remainder, or ZMod equality; decide correctness directions and any cost claim; and protect p=2 and truncated-subtraction boundaries. The canonical Lean expression, fingerprints, transports, and mutations remain downstream.
